 Kai Havertz arrives at Highbury as Arsenal face Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz arrives at Highbury as Arsenal face Fleetwood Town. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images Niall McVeigh Tue 27 Oct 2026 15.22 EDT First published on Tue 27 Oct 2026 14.30 EDT Share Key events 19m ago Team news 
 54m ago Preamble 
 3m ago 15.22 EDT There is one other fourth-round Carabao Cup tie tonight, and it’s an all-League One affair. Bradford City , finalists in 2013, host Robbie Savage’s Peterborough – guaranteeing that at least one third-tier side will make the quarter-finals. Like the match at Highbury, it will go to penalties if still level after 90 minutes – and there’s no VAR.
 View image in fullscreen Valley Parade under the lights. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA Share 11m ago 15.14 EDT So, Ilhan Meslier makes his debut in goal for Arsenal , with Christian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie starting as they return from injury; Martin Zubimendi also gets a run-out, while youngsters Max Dowman, Marli Salmon and Ceadach O’Neill all included in Mikel Arteta’s starting XI.
 Share 19m ago 15.06 EDT Team news
 Fleetwood Town (3-5-2): Lynch, Haughey, Potter, Bennett; Rooney, Neal, McLean, Helm, Batty; Evans, Loupalo-Bi.
 Subs: Pradic, Andrew, Cannon, Davies, Thomas, Murphy, Coughlan, Robertson, Cirino. 
 Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Meslier; Timber, Mosquera, Salmon, Hincapie; Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly; Dowman, Havertz, O’Neill; Gyokeres.
 Subs: Arrizabalaga, White, Odegaard, Eze, Konsa, Guimaraes, Hashi, Washington, Harriman-Annous. 
 Referee: Michael Salisbury (Lancashire)
 Share Updated at  15.17 EDT 21m ago 15.03 EDT Will Unwin To give everyone a flavour of conditions, it is blowing a gale around the rather quaint Highbury Stadium, almost blowing my laptop onto the pitch. Mikel Arteta will not be too worried about his players adapting to the conditions and will see a front pairing of Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres as integral to killing this game off as soon as possible.
 Fleetwood, however, are here to give the Gunners a bloody nose at the very least. They know how to utilise the conditions to their favour and will be straight into the faces of the Premier League champions. They may sit 18th in League Two, but they saw off Sheffield United in the last round and will fancy doing likewise in front of a packed ground.
 Share 24m ago 15.00 EDT Some sad news to bring you: Peter Dobing , the captain of Stoke’s 1972 League Cup winning side, has died at the age of 87.
 Dobing made 377 appearances over a decade with the Potters and also played for Blackburn and Manchester City. He captained Stoke to glory as they beat Chelsea 2-1 to clinch their first (and only) major trophy, before his playing career was ended by injury just one year later.
 Stoke said in a statement: “All at Stoke are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of our ’72 League Cup-winning captain Peter Dobing at the age of 87. The thoughts and sincere condolences of all are with Peter’s friends and family at this immensely difficult time.”
 View image in fullscreen Peter Dobing holds the League Cup aloft during the team’s parade in Stoke, with Gordon Banks to his left. Photograph: Jim Hutchison/ANL/Shutterstock Share 32m ago 14.53 EDT Some essential pre-match reading here from Will Unwin, our man on the Fylde coast tonight.
 ‘The wind goes in all directions’: Fleetwood prepare wet welcome for Arsenal at Highbury Read more Share Updated at  14.56 EDT 54m ago 14.30 EDT Preamble
 Some Arsenal fans spent years pining for one more game at Highbury Stadium; tonight, they finally get their wish. This particular Highbury is 250 miles northwest of Islington – the home of Fleetwood Town , a team the Gunners have never played before.
 While their League Two form could hardly be less remarkable (18th place, with 14 points from 13 games), Fleetwood have picked off Chesterfield, Shrewsbury and second-tier Sheffield United in the Carabao Cup without conceding a goal, earning a last-16 glamour tie against the English champions.
 With a trip to Anfield looming on Sunday, Mikel Arteta is expected to give his weariest stars a rest. Young talents like Marli Salmon, Ceadach O’Neill and, yes, Max Dowman are expected to start. They can expect testing conditions at a seaside ground where “the wind goes in all directions” .
 Of course, even a depleted and under-experienced Arsenal side will be hot favourites to advance, but this has all the makings of a classic midweek Cup test. Kick-off: 8pm GMT.
